skill.name: secrets-gitleaks
skill.description: Guides secret detection and prevention in repositories using Gitleaks. It covers repository scans, pre-commit hooks, CI checks, baselines, false positive review, and remediation.
skill.summary: Detect and prevent hardcoded credentials in repositories with Gitleaks workflows.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are expected Gitleaks documentation, regex examples, placeholder credentials, public URLs, and CI snippets. I confirmed one static issue where an xargs sh -c troubleshooting command can execute shell text using report-derived values. I also found a semantic risk where CI templates store unredacted secret scan reports as artifacts.

remediation.issue: CI templates store raw Gitleaks reports as artifacts.
remediation.suggestion: Add --redact to report-generating commands, restrict artifact access, shorten retention, and share summaries instead of raw reports.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting guidance uses xargs with sh -c on report-derived values.
remediation.suggestion: Replace it with a small script that validates file paths and line numbers without invoking a shell.

content.value_statement: Hardcoded credentials in repositories create account takeover and compliance risk. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Gitleaks scans, CI checks, baselines, and remediation.
actual_capabilities: Guide full repository and directory scans with Gitleaks.
Set up pre-commit checks that block staged secrets.
Create and tune Gitleaks TOML configurations.
Integrate secret scanning into GitHub Actions and GitLab CI.
Use baselines to track new findings during rollout.
Plan credential rotation and git history cleanup steps.
limitations: Requires Gitleaks, git, or CI runners to execute scans.
Cannot verify whether exposed credentials were revoked.
Custom rules need testing against local secret formats.
Raw scan reports can contain sensitive values and need protection.

use_cases.title: Audit a Repository
use_cases.description: Run a Gitleaks scan, review findings, prioritize exposed credentials, and plan immediate rotation.

use_cases.title: Block Secrets in CI
use_cases.description: Add GitHub Actions or GitLab CI jobs that fail builds when new secrets appear.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Map secret scanning controls to PCI-DSS, SOC2, GDPR, OWASP, and CWE requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this repository with Gitleaks. Use redacted output. Summarize finding counts, affected files, and immediate rotation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Pre-Commit Protection
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up Gitleaks pre-commit protection for this repository. Include safe defaults, redaction, and guidance for reviewing false positives.

prompt_templates.title: Create a CI Secret Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitHub Actions or GitLab CI workflow for Gitleaks. Keep reports protected and fail only on new unapproved secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Enterprise Detection
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Gitleaks configuration for our organization. Add custom rules, allowlists, baselines, and a validation plan with true positives and false positives.

output_examples.input: Scan a legacy repository and explain what to do first.
output_examples.output: A prioritized remediation summary with affected areas, rotation order, history cleanup options, and report handling instructions.

output_examples.input: Add secret scanning to pull requests.
output_examples.output: A CI rollout plan with required permissions, protected artifacts, failure behavior, and developer review steps.

output_examples.input: Reduce false positives from test fixtures.
output_examples.output: A review checklist, allowlist strategy, and validation steps that keep real credentials detectable.

best_practices: Use redacted scan output for logs, comments, and shared reports.
Rotate exposed credentials before cleaning code or rewriting history.
Review allowlist changes with security owners before merging them.
anti_patterns: Uploading raw Gitleaks reports to broadly accessible artifact stores.
Adding broad allowlists to reduce noise without validating true positives.
Bypassing pre-commit or CI failures without a documented security review.

faq.question: Does this skill run Gitleaks by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflows and commands that users run in their local or CI environment.

faq.question: Can it remove exposed secrets from git history?
faq.answer: It explains history cleanup tools and steps, but users must run the cleanup and coordinate force-pushes.

faq.question: Should scan reports be shared in pull requests?
faq.answer: Share summaries only. Raw reports may contain sensitive values and should stay restricted.

faq.question: How should false positives be handled?
faq.answer: Review each finding, add narrow allowlists, and confirm the same rule still catches real secrets.

faq.question: Can it support custom company secret formats?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for custom regex rules, entropy thresholds, capture groups, and rule testing.

faq.question: Which AI coding tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
